50290701.text: #We now arrive at the end of the parade of blessings. Let us offer {NICKNAME} our blessings one more time and give {M#him}{F#her} a resounding round of applause!

50290704.text: #That's a hero's welcome if Paimon ever saw one, {NICKNAME}!

50290705.text: You deserve it, of course! Considering the risk you took.

50290706.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Finally! I was looking everywhere for you!

50290707.text: Citlali! Why didn't you come to the parade?

50290708.text: Never mind that! I have something important to tell you. Come with me!

50290709.text: I went to revisit the revelations in my dreams as soon as you came back from battle.

50290710.text: But, I couldn't fall asleep just anywhere — I needed somewhere private. I didn't want anyone to overhear me sleep-talk or watch me contort myself into some weird position...

50290711.text: Anyway, that's not the important part! It's about Mavuika's death — her fate hasn't changed at all.

50290713.text: But, we both made it back!

50290714.text: Didn't you defeat the bad guy behind all this? Does that mean the war isn't over?

50290715.text: No, the disaster is over, but my dreams never lie...

50290716.text: That's why I came to find you. I need to know what I'm missing.

50290717.text: Where is Mavuika right now? Did she tell you what she's planning?

50290718.text: She said she was going to restore the Night Kingdom... Compared to fighting the Abyss, that should be pretty easy, right?

50290719.text: After all, the corrosion should be gone by now...

50290720.text: Easy... not so much. We can't restore the Ley Lines without the Lord of the Night, and I'm not sure she has enough power to do it on her own.

50290721.text: The Lord of the Night is weak right now. She told us that herself, remember? I'll admit — restoring the Ley Lines is simpler than reconstructing them entirely, but it's still no easy feat...

50290724.text: True... If the Lord of the Night could restore the Ley Lines by herself, all Mavuika would need to do is tell her we won.

50290725.text: Not even that. The Lord of the Night knows the Ley Lines better than anyone. I'm sure she knew of your victory before us all.

50290726.text: Point being, this matter is far more complicated than the Archon made it out to be. We need to get to the bottom of this.

50290727.text: But, why would she hide the truth from us?

50290728.text: Mavuika has accepted her death, remember? For her to let someone else dictate her end, there can be only one possibility...

50290729.text: She must think the outcome of her death... is worth it.

50290730.text: The moment Mavuika used the Ruler of Death's power, death was demanded in return — not necessarily as repayment for her aid, but as a "rule."

50290731.text: That means Mavuika doesn't have to just sacrifice herself to the Ruler of Death. She can still use her death to get something in return.

50290733.text: Then, let's get going! Where do you think she went? Could it be where we found the Source Mechanism?

50290734.text: The Lord of the Night should now be able to appear anywhere in Natlan. What we need to know is where the Ruler of Death can be summoned.

50290735.text: According to the Lord of the Night, the Ruler of Death is one of the shining Shades, an extremely elusive figure. Even woven scrolls dating back thousands of years have nearly no mentions of her.

50290901.text: I have grown weary of the endless wait. The fate of this land is of no interest to me anymore.

50290902.text: However, you humans managed to meet the expectations of the Heavenly Principles... For that result, you deserve praise.

50290903.text: Mavuika, as the price for using my power, I shall now bear witness to your death.

50290904.text: And with you, the war that your nation has waged for more than a thousand years shall meet its end.

50290906.text: Ah, you got here sooner than I expected.

50290908.text: Closing the final chapter on the plan that has consumed Natlan for five hundred... no, for the entirety of our history.

50290909.text: We've eradicated the Abyss from Natlan, but its power remains in worlds beyond Teyvat, tremendous and unyielding.

50290910.text: Only by completely restoring the Night Kingdom can we defend against its corrosion in the long run.

50290911.text: But, the architect of the Night Kingdom is near her end. She lacks the power for such a task.

50290912.text: Worse still, if her life force is depleted, the rules of Natlan disappear along with her.

50290913.text: We have no need for the Ode of Resurrection right now, but it remains Natlan's strongest defense should the Abyss return one day.

50290915.text: Yes, my plan is to once again place my life within the Sacred Flame.

50290916.text: Five hundred years ago, I gave my life for the chance to be reborn in this era.

50290917.text: A chance to see all my plans to completion. And now, to sustain the Lord of the Night, I will give my life once more.

50290918.text: I respect your decision, Mavuika, but this method requires an immense sacrifice.

50290919.text: The flames of your life force are exceedingly strong, but a life sustained by fire is one destined to die out one day. What will you do then?

50290920.text: I've thought about that... With the Abyss out of the picture for now, the Sacred Flame's power will be consumed at a much slower rate. My life force should be able to sustain it for another two or three hundred years.

50290921.text: Future Pyro Archons will continue to seek new sources of fire. As long as Natlan's legacy endures, the Night Kingdom will survive, impervious to the Abyss.

50290922.text: Once again, you place hope in the hands of the future...

50290923.text: But, the Pilgrimage can replenish the power of the Sacred Flame! We can give it that meaning! Why shoulder this burden by yourself?

50290924.text: Because, I want the Pilgrimage to change.

50290925.text: The Pilgrimage was an essential part of our struggle against the Abyss — a grand competition full of promise and glory. But, it also chained our people to an inescapable destiny.

50290926.text: Fear and anxiety have been our constant companions. We knew what the consequences would be if we laid down our arms. Morality left us with no other choice.

50290927.text: And so, Natlan became the nation of war.

50290928.text: This is where Xbalanque defeated the dragons and granted our people the liberation of their flesh. And now, in the same place, I have the chance to grant them the liberation of their spirit.

50290929.text: There will be no war, only competition — one fueled by our dreams for the future rather than a desperate struggle for survival.

50290930.text: A new future deserves a new meaning, a chance to take a definitive step forward.

50290932.text: Very noble indeed, but what does any of this have to do with you? You speak of duty, but not yourself.

50290933.text: In my eyes, Mavuika, you are not inherently special — a child of Natlan among countless others.

50290934.text: Yes, the situation is urgent and the Ley Lines must be restored right away, but it is too heavy a burden for you to shoulder alone.

50290935.text: That is where we differ, Lord of the Night. You see all humans as the same, but I understand what it means to be a leader.

50290936.text: A leader is swift and decisive in the face of reality.

50290937.text: Someone capable of making the "right choice" even when there are no good options on the table.

50290938.text: Sacrificing the remainder of my life to help Natlan overcome this crisis... That is the right choice.

50290939.text: After all, leadership is built on the trust of ordinary people. Without them, there is no Archon.

50290940.text: The people look to their leader to make the world a better place and stand up for them when it counts.

50290941.text: For that reason, I must see my duty through to the very end.

50290942.text: But, what about you, Mavuika? You still haven't talked about what you want...

50290943.text: Is it that unimportant to you?

50290945.text: There is nothing more important than protecting the future we built together!

50290946.text: (It's hard to argue with her logic. She probably knew we would come and prepared what to say in advance.)

50290947.text: (It's time for Natlan to enter a new era, and I know she wants to fulfill her duty as a "leader," but...)

50290948.text: (She deserves to have a place in the future she built with her people.)

50290949.text: I shall accept Mavuika's sacrifice for the Lord of the Night as her death, and I will bear witness to the very end.

50290950.text: Thus concludes the deal I made with Xbalanque several thousand years ago.

50290951.text: Lord of the Night, you may now begin.

50290954.text: There is another who wishes to take part in the ceremony, and I cannot disregard their intentions. I must wait for them to arrive.

50290956.text: *sigh* I was to bear witness to a death, and now the situation is increasingly tenuous.

50290957.text: If the life of this second individual fails to meet my requirements, I fear I may lose my patience.

50290958.text: Rest assured, his life will hold equal value. I am the helper of humanity, and I must always place their demands first, no matter who the human may be.

50290959.text: Hm, cumbersome, but there is nothing to be done — such is the duty of an angel.

50290962.text: Thank you for showing me the way.

50290964.text: The other individual you mentioned... It was him?

50290965.text: Indeed. Like you, he carries many lofty ideals.

50290966.text: Mavuika, I understand how you feel, and if I were an ordinary mortal, I would have no reason to stop you.

50290967.text: But, like you, I have been waiting for this day for too long, and I can offer a better solution.

50290968.text: You created this new future, and you deserve to guide its direction. Your life should not end here.

50290969.text: But, death... is the end I have been trying to reach all along. I have come this far to use my death to open the gates of the Ley Lines to my people.

50290971.text: Wait, the souls I saw in my dream?

50290972.text: That's right. They have been with me for the past five hundred years.

50290973.text: But, how!? Carrying that many souls within you... There's no way you could keep your consciousness intact!

50290974.text: Besides, you weren't affected by the Source Mechanism like I was.

50290975.text: Do you still remember the voice that you "heard"?

50290976.text: It came from my heart. With the help of technology from Khaenri'ah, my heart was modified to convert memories and souls from the Ley Lines into knowledge.

50290977.text: As a result, I became extremely sensitive to souls and developed the ability to sense their presence... much like yourself.

50290978.text: After encountering countless lost souls during the disaster five hundred years ago, I forsook the capacity for knowledge granted by the modification and used my heart as a vessel instead.

50290979.text: The lives of my comrades, as well as many Natlanese, have been stored here ever since.

50290980.text: And you want to... send them home?

50290981.text: Yes. The Ley Lines will not accept them. But, by merging my existence with the Lord of the Night, I can become master of the Ley Lines and change the rules entirely.

50290982.text: He expressed this to me, and I agreed.

50290983.text: The Captain envisions a kinder and fairer set of rules for humanity. In addition, he aims to challenge the authority of the Ruler of Death... In a word, his goal is revenge.

50290985.text: After all, it's because of her that I bear the curse of immortality, the curse of absolute life.

50290986.text: I now understand that which you seek...

50290987.text: Then, bear witness to my resolve and hatred.

50290988.text: The people of Khaenri'ah committed grave sins, and for that we were cursed to suffer endless physical torment, cursed to witness the demise of everything we held dear.

50290989.text: But, most of us were innocent. Most of us knew nothing of the Five Sinners' exploitation of Abyssal power... myself included.

50290990.text: If I sacrifice my life for the Lord of the Night, you get the death you desire. But, at the same time, the curse of immortality would negate the very death you seek.

50290991.text: Left unresolved, that paradox could uproot the natural order of this world... Even you, great Ruler of Death, lack the capacity to bear the consequences of that outcome.

50290992.text: Your curse is now the tool with which I will overturn the oppression of the gods. This is my challenge to you...

50290993.text: Forsake one of your rules — the choice is yours.

50291002.text: The curse of immortality still exists. Does that mean... The Captain will never move from this place?

50291003.text: Lord of the Night, is The Captain still with us?

50291004.text: There is no need to pursue traces of him. For those cursed with immortality, release from the mortal coil is the greatest form of peace.

50291005.text: Even so, please pass on my gratitude.

50291006.text: His long journey has finally come to a close. I suppose... this is a happy ending for him.

50291007.text: I cannot imagine how much pain he endured over the past five hundred years... or how much strength it took to never stray from his goal.

50291008.text: There's something I've been trying to figure out... I don't think I ever saw him sleep.

50291009.text: I tried to ask him about it on the way here, but he didn't answer. Just like always, he never talks about himself...

50291010.text: It's probably due to the voices.

50291011.text: When souls merge in a single being, their voices echo endlessly through the mind.

50291012.text: Souls that retain memories of their death often scream and wail in despair... Considering the number of souls inside him, that effect would be even greater.

50291013.text: So, over the past five hundred years, he didn't sleep... at all?

50291016.text: Without experiencing the curse of immortality, we will never truly know his agony.

50291017.text: But, I can see why his hatred for the Ruler of Death was so strong.

50291018.text: In the end, he used that immortality to his advantage and granted the Lord of the Night eternal life by fusing his existence with hers.

50291020.text: You may wonder why the Night Kingdom, a land of souls, was unable to accept the souls adrift on the surface...

50291021.text: The reason lies in the Heavenly Principles' modifications to the Ley Lines. The original purpose was to help counter the Abyss. And so, their stability was paramount.

50291022.text: But, at one point in time, Natlan's Ley Lines were decimated. Even after reconstruction, the rules needed for the Ode of Resurrection made it impossible to reconnect the Ley Lines to other nations.

50291023.text: That unique quality is precisely what drew The Captain to Natlan.

50291024.text: Did he try the same thing in other nations?

50291025.text: Yes, but all those attempts ended in failure.

50291026.text: He fought to save Natlan not only to defeat the Abyss, but because this is the only land where the souls within him could find salvation.

50291027.text: We met not long ago to talk about that very possibility, and I confirmed the feasibility of his plan.

50291028.text: I, too, recognized the need to change the rules of the Ley Lines, not only for the souls that wander this land, but for the outlanders that may perish here in the future...

50291029.text: In the eyes of the Heavenly Principles, that kind of change is extremely risky, if not impermissible... But, as an Angel, I have a duty to serve humanity — such is my mandate.

50291031.text: Citlali, when I gave you the Pilgrim's Chronicle, I said something rather pessimistic to you... Do you remember?

50291032.text: How many years of life are enough? Ten? One hundred? I thought it made no difference...

50291033.text: But, now, I have the chance to live forever. I am immensely grateful to humanity for this gift, and I am deeply sorry I thought so little of it in the past.

50291034.text: You don't need to thank us. You bear a heavy responsibility.

50291035.text: Heavy? No. That responsibility is the purpose of my existence.

50291036.text: Farewell, humans, creators of miracles. A new era awaits you.

50291037.text: Looks like she returned to the Night Kingdom.

50291038.text: So, this was The Captain's goal all along...

50291039.text: He fought to the end for all those souls and challenged the rules of the world in the process.

50291041.text: He took on a burden that was meant for me and even brought about a better outcome... It would seem I lost this duel.

50291042.text: He was right — Natlan needs a leader to guide its future. If not a successor, then that responsibility will continue to be mine to bear.

50291043.text: But, for now, let us pay our final respects to this fallen hero.

50299915.text: As the sun shines down on our nation...

50299918.text: There's a bunch of people waiting for you here, too!
